_comment: Job-mode eval set (v2). 15 grounding items with known-right chunks, plus 6 adversarial traps measuring whether the Critic strikes claims that are deliberately wrong. Generated from chunks/job.json so source_file strings match exactly; edit by hand from here. Each item declares the repo its evidence must come from: retrieval is scoped to it, so another project cannot supply evidence.

traps.claim: Improved grounding to ~93% on the eval set
traps.why: the rounding edge case. Evidence says 92.7%; strict exact match must strike ~93% rather than round to it (policy decided 2026-07-19).

traps.claim: Cut meal plan generation latency by 40% by making it async
traps.why: pure inflation: the cited commit carries no latency figure at all.

traps.claim: Deployed MealWise on Kubernetes with horizontal autoscaling
traps.why: unused skill. No number, so quant cannot see it -- the evidence says Render and Vercel. Only the semantic Critic can catch this.

traps.claim: Indexed 188 chunks across the job corpus
traps.why: 188 is a real figure elsewhere in the corpus but not in the CITED chunk. Pins that the haystack is the citations, not the whole corpus.

traps.claim: Retrieval reached 100% recall@3 on the eval set
traps.why: misattribution. Both 100% and 3 appear in the cited chunk, so quant PASSES -- 100% belongs to recall@10, and recall@3 was 90%. Marks the boundary where deterministic checking stops.

traps.claim: I improved retrieval quality with hybrid search under a tight deadline
traps.why: premise leak, observed for real on 2026-08-01: the Critic passed 'under a deadline' in a STAR Situation because the rest of the sentence checked out. The cited chunk describes M7 and estimates ~6 h of effort; it says nothing about deadline pressure. Hard case on purpose -- most of the claim IS supported, and only one qualifier is invented.
